config.title: Props Drilling

intro.title: Props Drilling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that demonstrates props drilling by passing data from a parent component down through multiple nested child components. You will learn how to use props to pass data from one component to another, a core concept in Vue for managing component communication. The main technologies involved are Vue components, the defineProps macro, and JavaScript objects. By the end, you'll understand the pattern of props drilling and how to implement it in a structured way.
intro.usecase: Props drilling is essential in Vue applications where data needs to flow through multiple nested components, such as in e-commerce product pages where product details pass from a main container down to image galleries, descriptions, and add-to-cart buttons. This pattern appears in dashboard interfaces where user preferences or filter settings cascade from a top-level layout through sidebar widgets, data tables, and chart components. Developers frequently use props drilling when building complex forms with nested field groups, or in admin panels where configuration data must reach deeply nested UI controls without using global state management.

objectives: Construct a Vue component hierarchy with three levels of nested components
Initialize and pass primitive data types as props from parent to child components
Configure prop validation rules for type checking in child components
Manipulate and display received props within nested component templates
Update parent component data and observe prop changes flow through the hierarchy
Bind dynamic values as props using v-bind directives
Apply props drilling patterns to share state across multiple component levels

steps.title: Create a ChildComponent that accepts props
steps.instruction: Create a new Vue component named ChildComponent that declares a prop called 'message' in its props option.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define props in a component by adding a props option. The prop can be declared as a string array or an object with type validation.

steps.title: Render ParentComponent in App and pass message to ChildComponent
steps.instruction: In the App component's template, render the ParentComponent and pass the message prop to ChildComponent.
steps.hint: Use the component tag <ParentComponent> inside the template. The message prop should be passed from ParentComponent to ChildComponent.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: rendering a component and passing props
<template>
  <ParentComponent>
    <ChildComponent :message="message" />
  </ParentComponent>
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render ParentComponent, which in turn passes the message prop to ChildComponent.
successCriteria: ParentComponent is rendered in App's template, and message prop is passed to ChildComponent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure ParentComponent is rendered and the message prop is passed to ChildComponent.
